chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf said: Ibn Abu Najran said, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman, on the authority of Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir, who said: I wrote by hand via Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) with several questions, among them: Inform me about Allah, the Mighty and High, whether He can be described with image and lineation? If you see fit, may Allah make me your ransom, write back to me with the correct view regarding Divine Unity.

So he (peace be upon him) wrote back to me, sending the letter via Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan: May Allah have mercy on you! You have enquired about Divine Unity and what your companions have ascribed. Allah is Greater than what is like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. Allah is Greater than the descriptions of the describers, those who compare Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with His creation, thus slandering Allah. And know, may Allah have mercy on you, that the correct view regarding Divine Unity is that which the Qur'an revealed regarding the attributes of Allah, the Mighty and High. Reject from Allah falsehood and anthropomorphism; there is neither negation nor comparison. He is Allah, the Firmly Present, the Existing. Allah is Greater than what the describers describe. Do not exceed the Qur'an, lest you go astray after the clear explanation has reached you.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct understanding of Divine Unity regarding Allah's attributes according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the core Shia doctrine of *la ta'tila wa la tashbih* (neither absolute negation nor anthropomorphic comparison), affirming Allah’s existence without reducing Him to created forms. It emphasizes that the Qur'an itself provides the sufficient framework for understanding Divine attributes, warning against over-interpretation that leads to deviation. The text underscores the transcendence of Allah above the limitations of human description and physical imagery.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 15. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: al-`Abbas ibn Ma`ruf said: Ibn Abu Najran said, on the authority of Hammad ibn `Uthman, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir that I wrote a letter, and sent it by hand via `Abd Al-Malik ibn A`yan to Abu `Abd Allah alSadiq (AS). In it, I asked about several issues, one of which was: “Please inform me about Allah, the Mighty and High. Can He be described with image and lineation? If this letter reaches you, may Allah make me your ransom, write back to me with the correct vies about Divine Unity.”

So he (AS) wrote back to me, sending the letter via `Abd al-Malik ibn A`yan: May Allah have mercy on you! You have enquired about Divine Unity. Allah is Greater than what your companions have ascribed. He is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, and there is nothing like unto Him. Allah is greater than the descriptions of the describers, those who describe Him inhuman terms, and those who compare Him with His creation, thus slandering Allah. Beware! May Allah have mercy on you! The correct view about Divine Unity is to be found in the attributes that Allah, the Mighty and High, revealed in the Qur`an. Reject anthropomorphism, and do not apply to Allah what is vain. Allah is Firmly Present. Allah is high above the descriptions of the describers. Do not exceed the Qur`an, as you will misled after the clear explanation has reached you.
